biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: inter-clade distances were very high, with values ranging from 13.0% to 21.4%

value: 91.5% clade A prevalence in non-Westernized vs 26.9% in Westernized

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: all four were significantly more prevalent in non-Westernized compared to westernized datasets
biomarker_value.notes: Values show dramatic differences between lifestyle populations

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable to this study design

ecog_performance_status.notes: Study does not assess ECOG performance status; participants were healthy individuals

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: 61.6% of non-Westernized individuals carried all four P. copri clades
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Study analyzed fecal metagenomes for P. copri genetic diversity and prevalence patterns

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not a clinical oncology study; this is a microbiome diversity study

value: 1,023 P. copri genomes reconstructed from >6,500 metagenomes
36 individual datasets from 6 continents and 25 countries
Four clades A, B, C, D named by decreasing genome abundance
Clade delineation time pre-dating human migratory waves out of Africa
P. copri diversity estimated to have begun ~6.5 million years ago
Analysis of ancient metagenomes from Iceman (5,300-year-old) and pre-Columbian coprolites
No strong associations found between P. copri clades and tested diseases
Multi-generational dietary modifications proposed as driver of reduced prevalence in Westernized populations
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: P. copri began to diversify (split of clade B) ∼6.5 million years ago
uncurated_metadata.notes: Major findings regarding P. copri complex evolutionary history and population structure

host_species.evidence_quote: Prevotella copri is a frequent inhabitant of the human intestinal microbiome
host_species.notes: Study focuses on P. copri in human gut microbiome across diverse populations

extraction_warnings: Granularity set to sample_level because paper includes three newly-sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) with multiple individual samples and families. Ancient samples also treated as distinct samples. Study also incorporated 36 public datasets with ~6,874 metagenomes, but these were not individually enumerated in the paper.

The paper analyzed publicly available datasets from multiple studies spanning different countries and diseases (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD). Individual samples from these public datasets are not listed with explicit IDs; thus only the newly-sequenced cohorts are represented as sample-level entries.
Age reported as study-level summary statistics (mean, SD, range) for Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania, and Madagascar cohorts; sample-level age not available, so study-level averages used.
Family role (child, mother, infant) noted as 'Mixed' for Ghana and Tanzania because the datasets included extended families but specific role assignments per sample were not tabulated in the paper.
Sequencing platform inferred as IlluminaHiSeq for newly-sequenced cohorts and HiSeq2500 for ancient samples based on methods; ancient Iceman samples sequenced on HiSeqX, recorded as IlluminaNextSeq.
Country field: Ethiopia, Ghana, Tanzania, Madagascar are non-Westernized populations sequenced in this study. Italy (Iceman) and Mexico (coprolites) are ancient samples.

Target_condition set to 'Health' because all newly-sequenced samples were from healthy individuals. Disease phenotypes were analyzed from public datasets but not as direct case samples in this study's collection.
Control field: Newly-sequenced cohorts treated as 'Study Control' (healthy baseline); ancient samples as 'Not Used' (not part of case-control design).

Westernized field: Set to 'No' for all newly-sequenced cohorts and ancient samples; publicly available datasets (which included both Westernized and non-Westernized populations) not individually enumerated.
Body_site: All samples are feces (stool or coprolites); Iceman sample also includes lower intestinal tract tissue.
DNA extraction kit: PowerSoil used for newly-sequenced cohorts; ancient samples used chloroform-based extraction method, coded as 'other'.
NCBI accession: PRJNA529124 (Ghana), PRJNA529400 (Tanzania), PRJNA504891 (Ethiopia), PRJEB31971 (ancient samples).
Age for ancient samples: Iceman ~5,300 years old; Mexican coprolites dated AD 673–768 (~1,320–1,350 years ago); these are expressed as approximate ages in years since deposition/death.
Ancestry: Native American ancestry inferred from PCA and mitochondrial haplogroup analysis for Mexican coprolites; not specified for modern African cohorts.
No explicit per-sample phenotype or disease association data provided; meta-analysis of disease cohorts was performed on publicly available datasets without individual sample enumeration.

Three new cohorts were sequenced (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) with basic demographic information only (age, sex, sample counts).
Age data are reported as group means and ranges, not individual sample ages.

Schema fields disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size_measurement, and tumor_size_residual_measurement are not relevant to this metagenomic diversity study, which does not involve clinical outcomes, patient performance status, or tumor measurements.
This study is not a clinical trial and does not measure individual patient outcomes. It is a population-level metagenomic analysis of P. copri genetic and functional diversity.
